scope: Explicit quarantine removal effects and per-attempt scratch derivation using existing signed lease fields; no Owner schema mutation
requirements: Removal contract freezes exact same-directory quarantine grammar, count one, parent checks, rename/recheck/owned unlink or no-replace restore, uncertainty preservation and directory fsync. Existing ordinary remover behavior stays unchanged.

Attempt scratch/quarantine names are a domain-separated deterministic function of existing signed lease pid, 64-hex nonce, phase, logical target and purpose; exact algorithm is frozen in effect recipe.
If names retain UUIDv4 grammar, explicitly derive its bytes and force version/variant bits from authenticated fields. Arbitrary per-attempt extra metadata cannot be added to the closed lease schema.
New lease pid equals actual native process pid before writes; retained old authenticated lease bytes/hash allow old-attempt name reconstruction after ESRCH recovery.
Immutable output-plan hash continues binding domain output bytes and paths; a new lease may change only its deterministic per-attempt scratch addresses.

Authenticated intended name is not entry ownership. Cleanup still requires exact dev/ino/birth identity from trustworthy native/durable evidence; unknown crashed entries are preserved/refused, not inferred owned by pid, age, ESRCH or contents.
Removal of the actual authenticated lease file uses its observed verified file identity; this does not authorize removing other entries derived from that lease.
counterexamples: Changed nonce/pid/target/purpose yields different bounded name and cannot retarget another attempt.
New lease with caller or dead pid refuses actual-process checks.
Valid authenticated old lease plus a foreign inode at derived scratch path never authorizes unlink.
Rename race preserves/restores foreign entries or reports uncertainty.
Resume retains original output-plan hash despite a new attempt lease.
Closed Owner lease schema rejects attempted extra scratch metadata fields.
qualification: Design and existing schema/remover source inspection only; no new implementation or runtime qualification claimed.
